_description: Known telemetry and data-exfiltration surfaces organized by platform. Each surface has a unique ID, probe method, closure method, and metadata.
_maintenance: Add new surfaces here as OS/browser updates introduce new telemetry channels. Remove surfaces that are no longer relevant.

os.name: Diagnostic Data (Telemetry Level)
os.description: Windows diagnostic and usage data sent to Microsoft. 'Full' level includes browsing history, app usage, and typed text.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection /v AllowTelemetry
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection /v AllowTelemetry /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
os.notes: Setting to 0 (Security) only available on Enterprise/Education SKUs. On Pro/Home, minimum is 1 (Basic). Setting still reduces data significantly.

os.name: Advertising ID
os.description: Unique per-device identifier used by apps to serve targeted ads. Resettable but re-enabled by default.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AdvertisingInfo /v Enabled
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AdvertisingInfo /v Enabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

os.name: Tailored Experiences
os.description: Microsoft uses diagnostic data to show personalized tips, ads, and recommendations within Windows.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Privacy /v TailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticDataEnabled
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Privacy /v TailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticDataEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
os.notes: Disabling removes personalized tips and ads in Windows interface.

os.name: Location Service
os.description: Windows and apps can access device location. System-wide location tracking.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\location /v Value
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\location /v Value /t REG_SZ /d Deny /f
os.notes: Disabling breaks map apps, weather location, find-my-device. Can be re-enabled per-app.

os.name: Activity History / Timeline
os.description: Windows records app launches, file access, and browsing activity. Synced across devices if Microsoft account is used.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System /v EnableActivityFeed
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System /v EnableActivityFeed /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
os.notes: Disabling removes Timeline feature and cross-device activity sync.

os.name: Cortana & Web Search Integration
os.description: Local search queries are sent to Bing. Cortana listens for voice activation and collects usage data.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Search /v BingSearchEnabled
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Search /v BingSearchEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
os.notes: Disabling stops web results in Start Menu search. Local file search unaffected.

os.name: Error Reporting
os.description: Windows Error Reporting sends crash dumps which may contain memory contents including PII.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting /v Disabled
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting /v Disabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
os.notes: Crash dumps won't be sent to Microsoft. You won't get 'check for solution' suggestions.

os.name: Find My Device
os.description: Periodically transmits device location to Microsoft for device tracking.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Settings\FindMyDevice /v LocationSyncEnabled
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Settings\FindMyDevice /v LocationSyncEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
os.notes: You won't be able to locate this device remotely if lost.

os.name: Typing & Inking Data Collection
os.description: Windows collects typing and handwriting patterns to improve recognition. Keystroke patterns are transmitted.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\InputPersonalization /v RestrictImplicitTextCollection
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\InputPersonalization /v RestrictImplicitTextCollection /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
os.notes: Autocorrect and text suggestions may become less accurate.

os.name: Wi-Fi Sense & Hotspot Sharing
os.description: Windows shares Wi-Fi credentials with contacts and automatically connects to suggested open hotspots.
os.probe_method: reg query HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WcmSvc\wifinetworkmanager\config /v AutoConnectAllowedOEM
os.closure_method: reg add HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WcmSvc\wifinetworkmanager\config /v AutoConnectAllowedOEM /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

chrome.name: Usage Statistics & Crash Reports
chrome.description: Chrome sends usage statistics, crash reports, and feature usage data to Google.
chrome.closure_method: Disable 'Make searches and browsing better / Send usage statistics and crash reports' in chrome://settings/privacy. Sets metrics_reporting and crash_reporting prefs.

chrome.name: Search & URL Suggestions
chrome.description: Characters typed in the address bar are sent to the default search engine for autocomplete suggestions.
chrome.probe_method: Check preference 'search.suggest_enabled' in Chrome profile Preferences file
chrome.closure_method: Disable 'Autocomplete searches and URLs' in chrome://settings/syncSetup. Sets search.suggest_enabled to false.
chrome.notes: You can still search by pressing Enter. Suggestions just won't appear as you type.

chrome.name: Enhanced Spell Check
chrome.description: Text typed in forms is sent to Google servers for spell checking. Basic spell check uses local dictionary only.
chrome.probe_method: Check preference 'spellcheck.use_spelling_service' in Chrome profile Preferences file
chrome.closure_method: Disable 'Enhanced spell check' in chrome://settings/languages. Switch to 'Basic spell check'.
chrome.notes: Basic spell check remains functional. Only Google-server-side checking is disabled.

chrome.name: Safe Browsing (Enhanced Protection)
chrome.description: URLs and file downloads are checked against Google's Safe Browsing database. Enhanced mode sends data in real-time and may include page content.
chrome.probe_method: Check preference 'safebrowsing.enabled' and 'safebrowsing.enhanced' in Chrome profile Preferences file
chrome.closure_method: Set Safe Browsing to 'Standard protection' or 'No protection' in chrome://settings/security. Standard still checks URLs locally against a downloaded list.
chrome.notes: Disabling entirely removes phishing/malware URL protection. Standard protection is a reasonable middle ground.

chrome.name: Chrome Sign-in & Sync
chrome.description: When signed into Chrome, browsing data (history, bookmarks, passwords, open tabs) syncs to Google account.
chrome.probe_method: Check if Chrome is signed in: look for 'account_info' in Local State file. Check sync state in Preferences.
chrome.closure_method: Sign out of Chrome or disable sync in chrome://settings/syncSetup. Can selectively disable sync categories.
chrome.notes: Disabling sync means bookmarks, passwords, and history won't sync across devices.

chrome.name: Password Manager Telemetry
chrome.description: Chrome's password manager reports usage patterns and may send password breach data.
chrome.closure_method: Disable 'Offer to save passwords' and 'Auto Sign-in' in chrome://settings/passwords
chrome.notes: You'll need to manage passwords manually or use a third-party password manager.

firefox.name: Firefox Telemetry & Studies
firefox.description: Firefox collects technical and interaction data. Studies may install experimental features.
firefox.probe_method: Check about:config prefs: toolkit.telemetry.enabled, datareporting.healthreport.uploadEnabled, app.normandy.enabled, app.shield.optoutstudies.enabled
firefox.closure_method: Disable 'Allow Firefox to send technical and interaction data' and 'Allow Firefox to install and run studies' in about:preferences#privacy

firefox.name: Crash Reports
firefox.description: Firefox sends crash reports to Mozilla which may include memory contents.
firefox.probe_method: Check about:crashes for submitted reports. Check pref: browser.crashReports.unsubmittedCheck.enabled

firefox.name: Search Suggestions
firefox.description: Characters typed in the search/address bar are sent to the search engine.

firefox.name: DNS-over-HTTPS (Default Resolver)
firefox.description: Firefox may route DNS queries through Cloudflare or another third party by default, bypassing system DNS settings.
firefox.probe_method: Check about:config pref: network.trr.mode (0=off, 1=reserved, 2=DoH first, 3=DoH only, 5=off by choice)
firefox.closure_method: Set network.trr.mode to 5 (off by choice) or 0 (off) in about:config. Alternatively configure a trusted DoH provider.
firefox.notes: DoH is privacy-positive if you trust the resolver. The concern is the default resolver choice. Consider switching to a privacy-respecting DoH provider rather than disabling.

firefox.name: Pocket Integration
firefox.description: Firefox integrates Pocket recommendations on the new tab page. Usage data is shared with Pocket (Mozilla-owned).
firefox.closure_method: Set extensions.pocket.enabled to false in about:config
firefox.notes: Removes Pocket recommendations from new tab page.

edge.name: Edge Diagnostic Data
edge.description: Edge sends diagnostic and usage data to Microsoft. Separate from Windows telemetry — both can be active simultaneously.
edge.probe_method: Check edge://settings/privacy for 'Optional diagnostic data' and 'Search and service improvement' settings
edge.closure_method: Disable 'Optional diagnostic data' and 'Improve search and services' in edge://settings/privacy

edge.name: Shopping & Price Comparison
edge.description: Edge sends browsing data to Microsoft for shopping recommendations and price comparisons.
edge.probe_method: Check edge://settings/privacy for 'Save time and money with Shopping in Microsoft Edge'
edge.notes: Removes price comparison popups and shopping notifications.

network.name: WebRTC IP Leakage
network.description: WebRTC can leak local and public IP addresses even when using a VPN. Affects all browsers.
network.probe_method: Check browser-level: Chrome: go to chrome://settings/privacy, Firefox: media.peerconnection.enabled in about:config
network.closure_method: Disable WebRTC in each browser: Chrome requires extension or flag. Firefox: set media.peerconnection.enabled to false.
network.notes: Disabling WebRTC breaks browser-based video/audio calling (Meet, Zoom web, Teams web).

network.name: DNS Leakage (System Resolver)
network.description: System DNS queries may go to ISP-assigned or default resolvers, leaking browsing domains.
network.probe_method: Run 'nslookup whoami.akamai.net' or check configured DNS servers via 'ipconfig /all'
network.closure_method: Configure privacy-respecting DNS (Quad9, Mullvad, or local) in network adapter settings or via DoH.
network.notes: Switching to Quad9 (9.9.9.9) or Mullvad DNS is recommended. Full prevention requires system-wide DoH/DoT.

os.name: Mac Analytics
os.description: macOS sends diagnostic and usage data to Apple. Includes crash reports, app usage, and system configuration.
os.probe_method: Check System Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements. Look for 'Share Mac Analytics' and 'Share with App Developers'.
os.closure_method: Disable 'Share Mac Analytics' and 'Share with App Developers' in System Settings. Also check /Library/Application Support/CrashReporter/

os.name: Apple Advertising & Personalization
os.description: Apple serves personalized ads in App Store, News, and Stocks based on device data and App Store activity.
os.probe_method: Check System Settings > Privacy & Security > Apple Advertising for 'Personalized Ads'
os.closure_method: Disable 'Personalized Ads' in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Apple Advertising
os.notes: You'll still see ads in the App Store — they just won't be targeted based on your activity.

os.name: Siri & Dictation Analytics
os.description: Siri interactions and dictation audio may be stored and reviewed by Apple for improvement.
os.probe_method: Check System Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements for 'Improve Siri & Dictation'
os.closure_method: Disable 'Improve Siri & Dictation' in System Settings. Also consider disabling Siri entirely in System Settings > Siri.
os.notes: Disabling Siri entirely removes voice assistant functionality.

os.name: Location Services
os.description: macOS provides location data to apps and system services. System-level location is used for Find My Mac and time zone.
os.probe_method: Check System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services
os.closure_method: Disable Location Services globally or per-app in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services
os.notes: Disabling globally breaks Find My Mac, automatic time zone, and map apps.

os.name: App Store & App Analytics Sharing
os.description: App developers may receive crash and usage data from your device. Third-party apps may also include their own analytics.
os.probe_method: Check System Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements for 'Share with App Developers'
os.closure_method: Disable 'Share with App Developers' in System Settings

safari.name: Safari Search & Safari Suggestions
safari.description: Safari sends search queries and partial address bar input to the selected search engine. Safari Suggestions may send data to Apple.
safari.probe_method: Check Safari > Settings > Search for 'Include Safari Suggestions' and 'Include search engine suggestions'
safari.closure_method: Disable both 'Include Safari Suggestions' and 'Include search engine suggestions' in Safari Settings > Search

safari.name: Safari Privacy Report Data
safari.description: Safari's Intelligent Tracking Prevention collects data about trackers. This data stays on device but contributes to Apple's tracker lists if shared.
safari.probe_method: Check Safari > Settings > Privacy for tracking prevention settings
safari.closure_method: Safari's ITP is privacy-positive and doesn't exfiltrate personal data. Recommend keeping enabled.
safari.notes: ITP is a privacy feature, not a privacy risk. This surface is flagged for awareness, not recommended for disabling.

network.name: WebRTC IP Leakage
network.description: WebRTC can leak local and public IP addresses even when using a VPN.
network.probe_method: Check Safari: enabled by default. Chrome/Firefox: check browser-level settings.
network.closure_method: Safari: no built-in disable. Use a browser extension or disable in other browsers. Chrome: flag or extension. Firefox: media.peerconnection.enabled=false.

network.name: DNS Leakage
network.description: System DNS queries may go to ISP-assigned resolvers. macOS uses the router/DHCP DNS by default.
network.probe_method: Check Network Settings > Advanced > DNS for configured DNS servers
network.closure_method: Configure trusted DNS servers in Network Settings or use a system-wide DoH/DoT profile.

surfaces._chrome_inherits: chrome surfaces from windows are OS-agnostic; same probe/closure applies on macOS
surfaces._firefox_inherits: firefox surfaces from windows are OS-agnostic; same probe/closure applies on macOS
surfaces._edge_inherits: edge surfaces from windows are OS-agnostic; same probe/closure applies on macOS

os.name: Ubuntu Report (popularity-contest)
os.description: Ubuntu can report installed packages and usage frequency to Canonical. Used for prioritizing package maintenance.
os.probe_method: Check if popularity-contest package is installed: dpkg -l popularity-contest. Check participation: cat /etc/popularity-contest.conf 2>/dev/null
os.closure_method: Remove popularity-contest: sudo apt remove popularity-contest. Or disable: sudo dpkg-reconfigure popularity-contest and select No.

os.name: Apport Error Reporting (Ubuntu)
os.description: Ubuntu's error reporting system collects crash dumps which may contain sensitive data.
os.probe_method: Check if apport is enabled: cat /etc/default/apport. Check service: systemctl is-active apport.service
os.closure_method: Disable apport: sudo systemctl stop apport.service && sudo systemctl disable apport.service. Edit /etc/default/apport: enabled=0.
os.notes: Crash reports won't be generated. You'll need to debug crashes manually.

os.name: Whoopsie Crash Reporter (Ubuntu)
os.description: Sends crash reports from Apport to Canonical's error database (daisy.ubuntu.com).
os.probe_method: Check if whoopsie is running: systemctl is-active whoopsie.service. Check if installed: dpkg -l whoopsie
os.closure_method: Remove whoopsie: sudo apt remove whoopsie. Or stop and mask: sudo systemctl stop whoopsie && sudo systemctl mask whoopsie.

os.name: GeoClue Location Service
os.description: Provides location services to desktop applications using nearby Wi-Fi networks and IP geolocation (Mozilla Location Service).
os.probe_method: Check if geoclue is running: systemctl --user is-active geoclue.service 2>/dev/null || pgrep -a geoclue
os.closure_method: Stop and mask the user service: systemctl --user stop geoclue.service && systemctl --user mask geoclue.service. Or remove: sudo apt remove geoclue-2.0
os.notes: Disabling breaks automatic timezone, weather apps that use location, and map applications.

os.name: Package Usage Metrics
os.description: Some distributions collect package usage statistics. On Fedora: DNF countme. On Ubuntu: optional popularity-contest. On Debian: popularity-contest.
os.probe_method: Fedora: check /etc/dnf/dnf.conf for countme=1. Ubuntu/Debian: check popularity-contest as above.
os.closure_method: Fedora: set countme=0 in /etc/dnf/dnf.conf. Ubuntu/Debian: remove or reconfigure popularity-contest.

brave.name: Brave Telemetry & P3A
brave.description: Brave collects anonymous privacy-preserving product analytics (P3A). No personal data but does report usage patterns.
brave.probe_method: Check brave://settings/privacy for 'Allow privacy-preserving product analytics (P3A)' and 'Automatically send daily usage ping to Brave'
brave.closure_method: Disable both P3A and daily usage ping in brave://settings/privacy
brave.notes: Brave's telemetry is already privacy-preserving by design. This is a conservative option for users who want zero telemetry.

brave.name: Brave Rewards & Ads
brave.description: If Brave Rewards is enabled, Brave serves privacy-preserving ads and collects attention data locally. Ad catalog is downloaded.
brave.closure_method: Disable Brave Rewards in brave://rewards if privacy is a higher priority than earning BAT.
brave.notes: Brave Rewards is privacy-respecting by design (local ad matching). This is optional for users who prefer zero ad interaction.

network.name: systemd-resolved DNS Configuration
network.description: systemd-resolved manages DNS and may use ISP/router-provided resolvers. Can leak DNS queries.
network.probe_method: Check active DNS: resolvectl status or systemd-resolve --status
network.closure_method: Configure DNS over TLS in /etc/systemd/resolved.conf: DNS=9.9.9.9#dns.quad9.net and DNSOverTLS=yes
network.notes: Recommended: Quad9 (9.9.9.9) or Mullvad DNS with DoT enabled.

network.name: WebRTC IP Leakage
network.description: WebRTC can leak local and public IP addresses even when using a VPN.
network.probe_method: Check browser-level settings for WebRTC. See platform-agnostic browser entries.
network.closure_method: Chrome/Brave: requires extension or flag. Firefox: media.peerconnection.enabled=false in about:config.

surfaces._chrome_inherits: chrome surfaces from windows are OS-agnostic; same probe/closure applies on Linux
surfaces._firefox_inherits: firefox surfaces from windows are OS-agnostic; same probe/closure applies on Linux
surfaces._edge_inherits: edge surfaces from windows are OS-agnostic; same probe/closure applies on Linux

_notes.shared_browsers: Chrome, Firefox, and Edge surfaces described under 'windows' are platform-agnostic and apply on macOS and Linux as well. The catalog uses inheritance markers to avoid duplication.
_notes.brave: Brave is listed under Linux but the surfaces apply to all platforms. Brave has minimal telemetry by design.
_notes.missing_platforms: ChromeOS, iOS, and Android are intentionally not included in v0.1. Their telemetry models differ significantly from desktop OSes.
_notes.how_to_add: To add a new surface: add an entry with unique surface_id under the appropriate platform/category. Include probe_method and closure_method that can be executed via shell/registry/file-check.
_notes.testing: Each probe_method should be testable with standard system tools. Each closure_method should be reversible or clearly documented as irreversible.
